title: Words You Can Build

concept.title: Compare the letter counts of a word with the supply
body: You have a pile of letters (some letters several times) and a list of words. A word can be built if for **every letter** the word needs no more copies than the pile has. Count the letters of the pile once. For each word count its own letters and compare letter by letter.
The pile is not used up between words: each word is checked on its own against the full pile. A letter missing from the pile has a supply of 0.

statement: You have a collection of letters, given as a word `chars` (a letter appearing twice means two copies). Each of the `n` given words is checked separately: it can be built if every letter is available at least as many times as the word needs it. Print the total length of all words that can be built.
inputFormat: The third line has the `n` words.
outputFormat: Print the total length of the words that can be built.
constraints: Each word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters.

examples.note: cat and hat can be built (3 + 3 = 6); bt needs a b; tree needs e.

hints: For each word count its letters and compare with the supply.
Add the length of the words that fit.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

chars = input().strip()
n = int(input())
w = input().split()

# Your code here

explanation: The supply of letters is counted once; each word is compared with it letter by letter.
solution.complexity: Time O(|chars| + total length), space O(alphabet).
